L125: ## Description
L126: 
L127: 【57†Magnus Ekhall (mekhall)】
L128: 
L129: opened 【58†on Nov 27, 2024】
L130: 
L131: Issue body actions
L132: 
L133: The CDF table in frodo1344.c has 7 entries amongst which one is 32765.
L134: 
L135: I noted that in the latest specification, table A.4 has only six elements. 32765 is missing.
L136: 
L137: Is that a typo in the specification or the implementation? (Or have I misunderstood something?)
L138: 
L139: Also in noise.c where the CDF table is used:
L140: 
L141: for (j = 0; j < (unsigned int)(CDF_TABLE_LEN - 1); j++) {
L142: the for loop does not use the last element of the CDF table. Is that intentional?
L143: ## Activity
L144: 
L145:   1. ### patricklonga commented on Nov 27, 2024
L146: 
L147: 【59†Patrick Longa (patricklonga)】
L148: 
L149: 【60†on Nov 27, 2024】
L150: 
L151: Contributor
L152: 
L153: More actions
L154: 
L155: It's a typo in Table A.4 in the specification. For FrodoKEM-1344, entry Tx(5) should be 32765 and entry Tx(6) should be 32767. This will be corrected.
L156: 
L157: And indeed, the last element in the CDF table is never accessed in the implementation.
L158: 
L159:   2. 【59†Patrick Longa (patricklonga)】

L26: Unidirectional Key Update in Updatable Encryption, Revisited Article
L27: 
L28: Authors: M. Jurkiewicz ; K. Prabucka
L29: In this paper we construct a new efficient updatable encryption (UE) scheme based on FrodoPKE learning with errors key encapsulation. We analyse the security of the proposed scheme in the backward-leak uni-directional setting within the rand-ind-eu-cpa model. Since the underlying computationally hard problem here is LWE, the scheme is secure against both classical and quantum attacks.
